correctness.rationale: For a selected 4-edge K_n subgraph H, an undominated outside pair is exactly a two-vertex transversal of H; any selected transversal would be isolated in the Kneser induced subgraph and contradict matching. Therefore paired domination is equivalent to vertex-cover number >=3 plus induced perfect matching. Decomposing all four-edge simple graphs into components leaves four cover-number-3 candidates, of which K3⊔K2 gives K1,3 in the disjointness graph, no perfect matching. Other three types have displayed perfect matchings and automorphism orders 4,16,384. No 2-set can dominate. Explicit exhaustive independent Python construction of KG(n,2), direct domination and recursive matching found optimum counts n4=1,n5=125,n6=180,n7=1575,n8=7665; the all-n classification follows from the structural proof, not this finite test. Complement-type census gives n5 orbit sizes 5,60,60.
